subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: What is the supported lifecycle for cron quarantine recovery archives after overflow: explicit Doctor-managed cleanup, an approved bounded retention policy, or no archive rotation?
rationale: The safe bound and deletion semantics for persisted recovery data are product and operations policy choices; the current code either silently retains data forever or would need to delete it automatically.

options.title: Doctor-managed cleanup
options.body: Retain archives for inspection, have Doctor report their count and size, and offer an explicit operator cleanup action.

options.title: Approved automatic retention
options.body: Adopt a documented archive count or age limit with focused upgrade and recovery-data tests.

options.title: Avoid archive recovery
options.body: Keep the bounded read/write failure behavior and require operator intervention for a saturated sidecar.

recommendation.title: Doctor-managed cleanup
recommendation.body: Retain archives for inspection, have Doctor report their count and size, and offer an explicit operator cleanup action.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows an explicit request for this decision-owner's review after retention became the outstanding concern.
